dicas.texto: Você sabe quantas vezes o 9 cabe dentro do 10?
Tente dividir o numerador pelo denominador. Quantos grupos inteiros de 9 você consegue tirar de 10?
Você tem 10/9. Isso é o mesmo que 9/9 mais quanto? Lembre-se que 9/9 é um inteiro.
Você tem 1 inteiro (9/9) e sobra uma fração. Qual é o numerador dessa sobra?
Se a reta está dividida em partes de 9, onde fica o número 1?
Localize o número 1 na reta. Como a fração é 10/9, você deve avançar uma marca após o 1.
Cada marca na reta representa 1/9. Se você está no 1 (que é 9/9), conte uma marca para a direita.
Coloque o ponto exatamente na primeira marca após o número 1.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 2 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 9 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

dicas.texto: A fraction has a top number and a bottom number. Focus on the number that tells how many parts are being considered.
Locate the number before the slash in the fraction from the problem, then enter it in the top box.
The numerator is the number written before the slash, not the number written after it.
Read the first number in the fraction and type that number in the upper field.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Locate the number after the slash in the fraction, then enter it in the bottom box.
The denominator is below the fraction bar, so it belongs in the lower field.
Read the second number in the fraction and type that number in the lower field.
Compare the number of parts being considered with the number of parts in one whole.
If the numerator is larger than the denominator, the fraction represents more than one whole.
The numerator is one more than the denominator, so the model must extend a little beyond one whole.
Use the fraction model with the given top and bottom numbers, then submit the displayed fraction showing more than one whole.
An improper fraction greater than one can be rewritten as whole units plus a remaining fractional part.
Divide the numerator by the denominator. The quotient is the whole-number part and the remainder becomes the new numerator.
Nine fits into ten once, leaving one part. Keep the denominator unchanged for the remaining fraction.
Enter the quotient as the whole part, the remainder as the fractional numerator, and keep the original denominator.
First locate one whole, then move a small fractional part to the right.
Divide the interval from 1 to 2 into nine equal parts and count one part after 1.
The target is just to the right of 1, much closer to 1 than to 2.
Start at 1 and select the first ninth mark to its right on the number line.
Before submitting, check that the fraction and its position on the number line represent the same amount.
Review the numerator, denominator, mixed-number form, and point placement in that order.
Make sure the point is just to the right of 1 and that all required fields are filled.
When the fraction, conversion, and number-line mark are ready, press the Done button to submit.

exercicio.statement:
Sean's baseball team played against Barry's team. The two teams were tied after nine innings, so the game went into extra innings. Sean's team won the game in the tenth inning. Usually a game only lasts nine innings, but since they played a tenth, Sean and Barry's game lasted 10/9 as long as a normal game. Show 10/9 on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?
